q-48022.name: Question 1
q-48022.problem: Using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}$ at $x=27$, approximate the value of $\sqrt[3]{28}.$
q-48022.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=27,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(27)+{f}^{′}(27)(x-27).
$$

Let's compute $f(27)$ and ${f}^{′}(27)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(27)=\sqrt[3]{27}=3,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt[3]{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(27)=\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{27}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{27}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
L(x)=3+\frac{1}{27}(x-27).
$$

We can approximate $\sqrt[3]{28}$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=28.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{28} & ≈L(28) \\  & =3+\frac{1}{27}(28-27) \\  & =3+\frac{1}{27}(1) \\  & =\frac{82}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Using the tangent line approximation of f(x)=x3 at x=27, approximate the value of 283.

a
289
b
7927
c
103
d
8227
e

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangent line approximation of f(x) at the point x=a is

L(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

In our case, we have a=27, which gives L(x)=f(27)+f′(27)(x−27).

Let's compute f(27) and f′(27) in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get f(27)=273=3, and computing the derivative, we get f′(x)=ddx(x3)=ddx(x1/3)=13x23, which in turn gives f′(27)=132723=127.

So, the tangent line approximation is L(x)=3+127(x−27).

We can approximate 283 by evaluating the tangent line approximation at x=28. We get 283≈L(28)=3+127(28−27)=3+127(1)=8227.

q-48026.name: Question 2
q-48026.problem: What is the tangent line approximation of $\sqrt[3]{x}$ at $x=8?$
q-48026.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=8,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(8)+{f}^{′}(8)(x-8).
$$

Let's compute $f(8)$ and ${f}^{′}(8)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(8)=\sqrt[3]{8}=2,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt[3]{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(8)=\frac{1}{3{(\sqrt[3]{8})}^{2}}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(8)+{f}^{′}(8)(x-8) \\  & =2+\frac{1}{12}(x-8) \\  & =2+\frac{1}{12}x-\frac{8}{12} \\  & =2-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{12}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+\frac{1}{12}x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-48026.html:
Question 2
?

What is the tangent line approximation of x3 at x=8?

a
L(x)=4+110x
b
L(x)=2+112x
c
L(x)=43+112x
d
L(x)=53−112x
e
L(x)=45+110x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangent line approximation of f(x) at the point x=a is

L(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

In our case, we have a=8, which gives L(x)=f(8)+f′(8)(x−8).

Let's compute f(8) and f′(8) in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get f(8)=83=2, and computing the derivative, we get f′(x)=ddx(x3)=ddx(x1/3)=13x23, which in turn gives f′(8)=13(83)2=112.

So, the tangent line approximation is L(x)=f(8)+f′(8)(x−8)=2+112(x−8)=2+112x−812=2−23+112x=43+112x.

q-86438.name: Question 3
q-86438.problem: Approximate the value of $\,2\sqrt[3]{8.9}\,$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)=2\sqrt[3]{x}\,$ at $\,x=8.$
q-86438.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=8,$ which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x)=f(8)+{f}^{′}(8)(x-8).\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute $f(8)$ and ${f}^{′}(8)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(8)=2\sqrt[3]{8}=4,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\sqrt[3]{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{1/3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

which in turn, gives

$$
{f}^{′}(8)=\frac{2}{3{(\sqrt[3]{8})}^{2}}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

So the tangent line approximation is

$$
L(x)=4+\frac{1}{6}(x-8).
$$

We can approximate $2\sqrt[3]{8.9}$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=8.9.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt[3]{8.9} & ≈L(8.9) \\  & =4+\frac{1}{6}(8.9-8) \\  & =4+\frac{1}{6}(0.9) \\  & =4+0.15 \\  & =4.15\,.\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent line approximation of f(x) at the point x=a is

L(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

In our case, we have a=8, which gives

L(x)=f(8)+f′(8)(x−8).

Let's compute f(8) and f′(8) in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get f(8)=283=4, and computing the derivative, we get f′(x)=ddx(2x3)=ddx(2x1/3)=23x23, which in turn, gives f′(8)=23(83)2=16.

So the tangent line approximation is

q-348182.name: Question 4
q-348182.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=36,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(36)+{f}^{′}(36)(x-36).
$$

Let's compute $f(36)$ and ${f}^{′}(36)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(36)=\sqrt{36}=6,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}},
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(36)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{36}}=\frac{1}{2\cdot 6}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(36)+{f}^{′}(36)(x-36) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12}(x-36) \\  & =6+\frac{1}{12}x-3 \\  & =6-3+\frac{1}{12}x \\  & =3+\frac{1}{12}x.\end{aligned}
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$

which in turn gives

$$

$$

$$
L(x)=1+\frac{1}{2}(x-1).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & ≈L(2) \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2}(2-1) \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
